programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Dan & Gran
programme.desc: Grumblestunk's new speed camera catches Stan breaking the speed limit on his scooter, but he can't have been! Stan and Gran have to clear his name! Tha an camara luaiths ùr aig Greannarlobht a' glacadh Dan 's e a' briste an casg-astair air an sgùtair aige, ach cha ghabh seo a chreidsinn! Feumaidh Dan is Gran a dhearbhadh neoihiontach!

programme.title: Beathaichean a’ Bocadaich
programme.desc: Tha Sophie a’ coimhead tron phrosbaig sheunta aice airson faicinn ciamar a bhios beathaichean a’ bocadaich. Tha i ag ionnsachadh mar a bhios diofar bheathaichean a’ gluasad agus cuide ri a caraidean, tha i a’ cruthachadh dannsa. An-diugh, danns coltach ri cearc agus sìota! Sophie looks through her magic binoculars to find out how animals boogie. She learns how different animals dance and, along with her friends, creates a dance using animal movements. Join her and dance like a chicken and a cheetah!

programme.title: Meaban and Moo
programme.desc: Tha Linda a’ tadhal air a caraidean Meaban is Moo gus innse dhaibh mu chuirm a chunnaic i. Tha seo gam brosnachadh gus cuirm shònraichte a chur air dòigh dhithse agus, às dèidh beagan ullachaidh, tha iad deiseil airson a thoirt chun an àrd-ùrlair. Linda visits her friend Meaban and Moo to tell them about her trip to the theatre. This gives them the idea to put on a concert for Linda and the stage is soon set for a very special performance!

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha ’ad uile air chrith leis an fhuachd air Planaid nan Clangairean – cho fuar ‘s gum b’ fheudar fiù 's dhan Chearc Iarainn dèanamh air Uamh nan Clangairean 'son cumail blàth. Nach math g’ eil Granaidh comasach is taiceil san t-suidheachadh seo! Everyone is shivering with the cold on the Planet, so cold that even the Iron Chicken has had to go to the cave to get warm. Fortunately, Granny proves to be helpful.

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha a’ Chearc Iarainn ag innse do Mheanbh gu bheil rudeigin a’ tighinn. Tha Meanbh ’son faighinn a-mach dè tha tighinn. Abair gum bi an t-iongnadh mìorbhaileach nuair a thig e! The Iron Chicken tells Tiny that something is coming. Tiny wants to find out what it is. What a marvellous surprise when it does indeed appear!

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Siobhan NicAonghais a’ leughadh Bilidh agus an Dràgon. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Nadia Shireen agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. A bedtime story for young children. Siobhan MacInnes reads Bilidh agus an Dràgon, written by Nadia Shireen and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod.

programme.title: Clann Na Cruinne
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Hikari ‘son rìs fhàs, tha Mgr. Yamanaka, fear a th' air a bhith na thuathanach rìs còrr is caogad bliadhna, dha comhairleachadh. Tha a’ chùis a’ còrdadh rithe ’s tha i a co-dhùnadh gum bi i na tuathanach rìs nuair a dh' fhàsas i mòr. When Hikari wants to grow rice, she gets advice from Mr Yamanaka, who’s been a rice farmer for over 50 years. The process is so enjoyable that Hikari decides she wants to be a rice farmer when she grows up.

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Tha Sebastian dol a theagasg an clas an-diugh air a’ bheinn ‘s tha e dol a dhearbhadh gu bheil e cho eòlach air na beanntan ‘s nach eil feum air a dhol dhan sgoil. Today’s class is going to be taught by Sebastian on the mountain and he is going to prove that his knowledge is so vast that he doesn’t need to go to school.

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha an Treud a' cluinntinn bhana nan reòiteagan air fàire agus a' tighinn an àrd le plana faighinn thuice. Leis an dràibhear a' faighinn cuideachadh, tha na caoraich air an dòigh le reòiteagan gun chrìoch - ach saoil am faigh daoine a-mach dè rinn iad? The flock hear the enticing tunes of an ice cream van approaching and quickly hatch a plan to divert it into their field. While the driver seeks help, the flock have great fun with an endless supply of ice cream. But will they be able to cover their tracks before they're discovered?

programme.title: Uaine
programme.desc: An do smaoinich thu riamh mu càit am bi sgudal a’ dol? Tha Calum airson na ceist sin a fhreagairt agus anns a’ phrògram seo, tha e a’ tadhal air Ionad Ath-chuartachaidh Polmadie airson faghinn a-mach dè a tha a’ tachairt dhan sgudal a th’ anns na bionaichean uaine ann am baile Ghlaschu. Have you ever thought about where your rubbish goes? Calum wants to find out more and visits Polmadie Recycling Centre to find out what happens to green bin waste from Glasgow City.

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Tha Bonns den bheachd gu bheil na Gumbalan mòra nas fheàrr air cleasan – ‘s e sin gus an do dh'fheuch i air an dùbhlan as dorra ‘Nas Fheàrr A-Mach Seach A-Steach’! Bounce thinks that the bigger Gumbles are better at tricks - that is until she tries the most difficult challenge ‘Better Out Than In’!

programme.title: Miann na Maighdinn-mara/Mermaid Tales
programme.desc: Kate comes across an interesting sea creature, known as a sunfish, which is native to tropical waters but is likely to have been carried to the islands by the Gulf Stream.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Eilidh Cameron Sykes from Ballachulish joins Joy in the studio to talk about her business, and Calum Maclean visits a famous industrial village in Lanarkshire.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Port Steòrnabhaigh
programme.desc: Based in the main port in the Hebrides, we follow the beating hearts of Stornoway Harbour. In her shelter, there is a bustling community to be found. In this episode, preparation works are full steam ahead at Stornoway’s new Deep Water Terminal, and we meet some American residents who take shelter in the harbour over the winter. Stèidhte ann am prìomh port nan Eilean Siar, the sinne a’ leantainn cridhe Port Steòrnabhaigh. Na fasgadh, tha coimhearsnachd trang ri lorg. Anns a’ phrògram seo, tha obair ullachaidh a’ dol aig a’ Chala Dhomhain ùr ann an Steòrnabhagh, ‘s coinnichidh sinn ri dithis Aimeireaganach a th’ ann an samhailteach a’ chala fad a’ gheamhraidh. Thig còmhla rinn ‘s sinn a’ leanntainn beatha ann am Port Steòrnabhaigh.

programme.title: Mise is ADHD
programme.desc: Tha Siùsaidh NicDhonnchaidh a coinneachadh daoin’ eile le ADHD. Suzie Roberts shares experiences with others who have ADHD.

programme.title: Dàna | Scotland's Wild Side
programme.desc: Suidhichte taobh a-staigh Cearcall na h-Artaig, tha Eileanan Lofoten ann an Nirribhidh a’ tabhann luach fad-beatha de thoileachas don luchd-turais a bhitheas a’ tadhal ann. Air a tharraing leis an t-sreap agus an surfadh air leth a tha ri fhaotainn ann, tha Coinneach MacFhraing a’ siubhal timcheall nan eilean còmhla ri a chompanach, Calum Gibb, gus eòlas fhaighinn air an t-àite miorbhaileach seo. Situated within the Arctic Circle, Norway’s Lofoten islands offer a lifetime’s worth of exploration in the outdoors. Attracted by the world-class climbing and surfing on offer, Coinneach Rankin journeys around the islands with his companion, Calum Gibb, to glean unique experiences.

programme.title: Ciad-fàthan nan Creutairean/Wild Senses
programme.desc: We explore the surprising ways animals use touch to sense their world, find food and stay out of danger.

programme.title: Brunch le Abigail
programme.desc: Cumaidh Bircher Muesli a’ dol thu fad na maidne, agus air a stòradh sa frids, faodar a chumail airson latha no dhà! A Bircher muesli will keep you going all morning, and by being stored in the fridge it will stretch for a few days! In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Port
programme.desc: Prògram aithriseach ciùil le Julie Fowlis is Muireann NicAmhlaoibh. Nì Port taisbeanadh air na ceanglaichean dualchais a tha eadar an dithis aca. An t-seachdain-sa tha Julie agus Muireann a' tadhal air Siorrachd Chiarri agus còmhla riutha, tha dithis a Alba; an sàr sheinneadair Seumas Greumach agus a neach-ciùil barraichte, Iain MacPhàrlain a Gleann Fhionnain. Bha Siorrachd Chiarri a-riamh ainmeil airson luchd-ciùil agus tha na seòid a'coinneachadh ris na chòmlain Lumiere agus Cuas; agus ri Pádraig Ó Sé airson còmhradh agus, gu nadurrach, airson stùr a chuir a puirt. Musical documentary presented by Julie Fowlis and Muireann NicAmhlaoibh. Port reveals their shared musical heritage and in this episode Julie and Muireann visit Co Kerry. Accompanying them from Scotland are renowned singer James Graham and the brilliant Glennfinnan musician, Iain MacFarlane. The south west of Ireland and Co Kerry have long been noted for the calibre of their musicians - we meet the bands Lumiere and Cuas, plus Pádraig Ó Sé for some craic and lively musical sessions.

programme.title: India: Nature's Wonderland
programme.desc: The hidden wonders of India's spectacular natural world are revealed by wildlife expert Liz Bonnin, actress Freida Pinto and mountaineer Jon Gupta. Experience a village of birds, masks that come alive, the world's greatest mountain range and baby turtles erupting out of the sand. This is truly a land like no other.

programme.title: From Ice to Fire: The Incredible Science of Temperature
programme.desc: Dr Helen Czerksi explores the extraordinary science of heat. She reveals how heat is the hidden energy contained within matter, with the power to transform it from one state to another. Our ability to harness this fundamental law of science has led to some of humanity's greatest achievements, from the molten metals that enabled us to make tools, to the great engines of the Industrial Revolution powered by steam, to the searing heat of plasmas that offer almost unlimited power.

programme.title: Murder on the Victorian Railway
programme.desc: London 1864. On a Hackney bound train, a guard discovers blood in a first-class carriage - and a body on the railway embankment. For the first time, a murder has taken place on Britain's railways. Over a hundred years later, this single documentary for BBC Two uses the first-hand testimony of the people involved at the time to explore this unique event and how it provoked a huge public outcry and debate. The story quickly became a news sensation as the dangers of the brave new world of the train were laid bare. Over a hundred years later, the witnesses to this story may be long dead but their words survive in court transcripts, memoirs, letters and vivid journalism. These testimonies are now used to tell the story, taking the documentary deep into the 19th century to meet an extraordinary cross section of real-life Victorian London - from the engine driver who found the body to the detective in charge of the investigation. Who killed Mr Briggs?

programme.title: A Very Peculiar Practice
programme.desc: Stephen finds an enemy and then a friend when he tries to help the appropriately named Professor Furie overcome his tiredness.

programme.title: A Very Peculiar Practice
programme.desc: The medical staff must write academic research papers. Bob seizes the opportunity to trial a tranquiliser that might kick off his career as a private consultant.

programme.title: Timeshift
programme.desc: What happens when a literary novelist tries to write popular romantic fiction? To mark 100 years of romance publishers Mills and Boon, literary novelist Stella Duffy takes on the challenge of writing for them. Romantic fiction is a global phenomenon, and Mills and Boon are among the biggest names in the business. The company welcomes submissions from new authors, but as Duffy soon finds out, writing a Mills and Boon is harder than it looks. Help is at hand from the publishers themselves, a prolific Mills and Boon author and some avid romance fans, as Duffy's quest to create the perfect romantic novel takes her from London to Italy on a journey that is both an insight into the art of romantic fiction and the joy and frustration of writing itself.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: When a viewer contacts Rip Off Britain after suspecting the online task work he’s been completing might not be for real, the team investigate the sophisticated world of so-called task scams. Plus justice for the victims of one dodgy spray foam insulation firm. Seven years after Rip Off Britain went undercover as a sales operative, the team hear how that footage formed part of the investigation that put the man responsible behind bars.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is overcome by the amount of beige on show in a Telford flat. Dion heads downwards to reveal an unexpected bonus in Leeds. In Suffolk, there are character features for Jacqui to uncover.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: A well-groomed Charlie Ross pays a visit to a barbershop museum in Norfolk to see a huge collection of antique shaving mugs. One scuttle-shaped mug was patented in around 1867. In total, proud museum owner Richard Finney has 500 on display. Aiming to shave off a few pounds on their purchases are two teams of families shopping at a massive antiques centre in King’s Lynn. In red are father and daughter Simon and Ellen, and in blue are father and son Dave and James. With maths teacher Ellen keeping tabs on the reds’ budget, scientist Simon hopes their chemistry will generate profits. Meanwhile, the blues have a close encounter with a model of E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, but at £245, he’s not coming home with them. Wielding his gavel in neighbouring Lincolnshire is auctioneer Colin Young. He shares his estimates with Charlie before the teams’ items go under the hammer. Profit or loss, one team comes out on top – but which one?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Natalie Cassidy: Caring Together
programme.desc: Natalie’s juggling college and family life, learning about teenage mental health, online pressures and autism - and how care reaches far beyond the classroom.

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: The Rev Richard Coles joins Robson to explore the Northumberland coastline. They take a Canadian canoe trip along the River Coquet, visit the hidden gem of Walkworth's secret hermitage, make the crossing to Lindisfarne for a photography class and have a go at rope work.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: In Somerset, Micky from the busy seaside town of Hove is ready to fulfil a long-held dream of escaping to the countryside. She wants a property with lots of land for her big, beloved rescue dog, and Jules Hudson is there to answer her prayers with a line-up of standout properties that fit the bill. Jules also tries his hand at traditional screen printing when he visits a small studio specialising in designs inspired by nature.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie and Flo head to Shrewsbury to help James and his sister Maria transform his plain, uninspired garden into a Doctor Who-inspired sci-fi dream. With little more than a fence, a small shed and a table and chairs, the space is ready for a complete regeneration! A lifelong Doctor Who and sci-fi fan, James envisions a low-maintenance, alien-themed haven complete with a TARDIS-style shed, futuristic planting, a circular pathway and a tranquil water feature. With Maria’s support and Charlie and Flo’s creativity, can this ordinary garden be turned into an otherworldly escape, all on a £5,000 budget? James, who has Asperger’s syndrome, has been living independently in his own home since the passing of their father in 2021. His sister Maria and her husband live just a mile away, and together they form a close-knit and supportive family. James’s lifelong passion for classic Doctor Who and all things sci-fi has inspired this ambitious project, a fun, thematic garden where he can relax, enjoy nature and truly feel at home in his very own alien world.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Anna, Gemma, Zoe and Andreas – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns - but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Ria Lina. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: After solving the Andie Bell case, Pip is forced to confront the consequences of what her investigation exposed. It may have cleared Sal’s name, but it tore Cara’s family apart, and the guilt weighs heavily on Pip. In an attempt to rebuild her relationship with Cara, Pip releases a podcast to tell the world the real story. The only person yet to face justice is Max Hastings, and as his trial approaches, Pip is determined to help his victims find closure. However, the prosecution’s case begins to falter when Becca Bell withdraws from testifying. Unwilling to accept this, Pip musters the courage to visit Becca in prison with the hope of convincing her that giving evidence still matters. Pip wants to focus on supporting Ravi at the upcoming memorial for his brother, but when a mysterious note promising information on Max appears in her locker, Pip must make a difficult decision. Little Kilton comes together to say goodbye to both Andie Bell and Sal Singh. The end of one dark chapter gives way to another, as Cara finds herself in a dangerous situation, and Jamie Reynolds, Connor’s brother and a key witness in Max’s trial, disappears without warning.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip hits a dead end and rethinks. Digging into Jamie’s recent behaviour and last movements, she realises he may not be an innocent victim after all.

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon, Lee Mack and David Mitchell return in an episode packed with some of the best bits from series 19. A stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal amazing stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Among the guests joining Lee Mack and David Mitchell are Lucy Beaumont, Bob Mortimer, Jamelia, John Kearns, Harriet Kemsley, Yinka Bokinni, Gyles Brandreth, Dianne Buswell, Mark Chapman, Montell Douglas, Tasha Ghouri, Julie Hesmondhalgh, Will Kirk, David Morrissey, Josh Pugh and Holly Willoughby.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: When a viewer contacts Rip Off Britain after suspecting the online task work he’s been completing might not be for real, the team investigate the sophisticated world of so-called task scams. Plus justice for the victims of one dodgy spray foam insulation firm. programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is overcome by the amount of beige on show in a Telford flat. Dion heads downwards to reveal an unexpected bonus in Leeds. In Suffolk, there are character features for Jacqui to uncover.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: A well-groomed Charlie Ross pays a visit to a barbershop museum in Norfolk to see a huge collection of antique shaving mugs. One scuttle-shaped mug was patented in around 1867. In total, proud museum owner Richard Finney has 500 on display. Aiming to shave off a few pounds on their purchases are two teams of families shopping at a massive antiques centre in King’s Lynn. In red are father and daughter Simon and Ellen, and in blue are father and son Dave and James. With maths teacher Ellen keeping tabs on the reds’ budget, scientist Simon hopes their chemistry will generate profits. Meanwhile, the blues have a close encounter with a model of E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, but at £245, he’s not coming home with them. Wielding his gavel in neighbouring Lincolnshire is auctioneer Colin Young. He shares his estimates with Charlie before the teams’ items go under the hammer. Profit or loss, one team comes out on top – but which one?

Wielding his gavel in neighbouring Lincolnshire is auctioneer Colin Young. He shares his estimates with Charlie before the teams’ items go under the hammer. Profit or loss, one team comes out on top – but which one?

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie and Flo head to Shrewsbury to help James and his sister Maria transform his plain, uninspired garden into a Doctor Who-inspired sci-fi dream. With little more than a fence, a small shed and a table and chairs, the space is ready for a complete regeneration! A lifelong Doctor Who and sci-fi fan, James envisions a low-maintenance, alien-themed haven complete with a TARDIS-style shed, futuristic planting, a circular pathway and a tranquil water feature. With Maria’s support and Charlie and Flo’s creativity, can this ordinary garden be turned into an otherworldly escape, all on a £5,000 budget? James, who has Asperger’s syndrome, has been living independently in his own home since the passing of their father in 2021. His sister Maria and her husband live just a mile away, and together they form a close-knit and supportive family. James’s lifelong passion for classic Doctor Who and all things sci-fi has inspired this ambitious project, a fun, thematic garden where he can relax, enjoy nature and truly feel at home in his very own alien world.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Anna, Gemma, Zoe and Andreas – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: After solving the Andie Bell case, Pip is forced to confront the consequences of what her investigation exposed. It may have cleared Sal’s name, but it tore Cara’s family apart, and the guilt weighs heavily on Pip. In an attempt to rebuild her relationship with Cara, Pip releases a podcast to tell the world the real story. The only person yet to face justice is Max Hastings, and as his trial approaches, Pip is determined to help his victims find closure. However, the prosecution’s case begins to falter when Becca Bell withdraws from testifying. Unwilling to accept this, Pip musters the courage to visit Becca in prison with the hope of convincing her that giving evidence still matters. Pip wants to focus on supporting Ravi at the upcoming memorial for his brother, but when a mysterious note promising information on Max appears in her locker, Pip must make a difficult decision. Little Kilton comes together to say goodbye to both Andie Bell and Sal Singh. The end of one dark chapter gives way to another, as Cara finds herself in a dangerous situation, and Jamie Reynolds, Connor’s brother and a key witness in Max’s trial, disappears without warning.

programme.desc: Charlie and Flo head to Shrewsbury to help James and his sister Maria transform his plain, uninspired garden into a Doctor Who-inspired sci-fi dream. With little more than a fence, a small shed and a table and chairs, the space is ready for a complete regeneration! A lifelong Doctor Who and sci-fi fan, James envisions a low-maintenance, alien-themed haven complete with a TARDIS-style shed, futuristic planting, a circular pathway and a tranquil water feature. With Maria’s support and Charlie and Flo’s creativity, can this ordinary garden be turned into an otherworldly escape, all on a £5,000 budget? James, who has Asperger’s syndrome, has been living independently in his own home since the passing of their father in 2021. His sister Maria and her husband live just a mile away, and together they form a close-knit and supportive family. James’s lifelong passion for classic Doctor Who and all things sci-fi has inspired this ambitious project, a fun, thematic garden where he can relax, enjoy nature and truly feel at home in his very own alien world.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Anna, Gemma, Zoe and Andreas – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: A well-groomed Charlie Ross pays a visit to a barbershop museum in Norfolk to see a huge collection of antique shaving mugs. One scuttle-shaped mug was patented in around 1867. In red are father and daughter Simon and Ellen, and in blue are father and son Dave and James. With maths teacher Ellen keeping tabs on the reds’ budget, scientist Simon hopes their chemistry will generate profits. Meanwhile, the blues have a close encounter with a model of E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, but at £245, he’s not coming home with them. Wielding his gavel in neighbouring Lincolnshire is auctioneer Colin Young. He shares his estimates with Charlie before the teams’ items go under the hammer. Profit or loss, one team comes out on top – but which one?

programme.title: Escape to the Country

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie and Flo head to Shrewsbury to help James and his sister Maria transform his plain, uninspired garden into a Doctor Who-inspired sci-fi dream. With little more than a fence, a small shed and a table and chairs, the space is ready for a complete regeneration! A lifelong Doctor Who and sci-fi fan, James envisions a low-maintenance, alien-themed haven complete with a TARDIS-style shed, futuristic planting, a circular pathway and a tranquil water feature. With Maria’s support and Charlie and Flo’s creativity, can this ordinary garden be turned into an otherworldly escape, all on a £5,000 budget? James, who has Asperger’s syndrome, has been living independently in his own home since the passing of their father in 2021. His sister Maria and her husband live just a mile away, and together they form a close-knit and supportive family. James’s lifelong passion for classic Doctor Who and all things sci-fi has inspired this ambitious project, a fun, thematic garden where he can relax, enjoy nature and truly feel at home in his very own alien world.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Anna, Gemma, Zoe and Andreas – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: The Rev Richard Coles joins Robson to explore the Northumberland coastline. They take a Canadian canoe trip along the River Coquet, visit the hidden gem of Walkworth's secret hermitage, make the crossing to Lindisfarne for a photography class and have a go at rope work.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: In Somerset, Micky from the busy seaside town of Hove is ready to fulfil a long-held dream of escaping to the countryside. She wants a property with lots of land for her big, beloved rescue dog, and Jules Hudson is there to answer her prayers with a line-up of standout properties that fit the bill. Jules also tries his hand at traditional screen printing when he visits a small studio specialising in designs inspired by nature.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie and Flo head to Shrewsbury to help James and his sister Maria transform his plain, uninspired garden into a Doctor Who-inspired sci-fi dream. With little more than a fence, a small shed and a table and chairs, the space is ready for a complete regeneration! A lifelong Doctor Who and sci-fi fan, James envisions a low-maintenance, alien-themed haven complete with a TARDIS-style shed, futuristic planting, a circular pathway and a tranquil water feature. With Maria’s support and Charlie and Flo’s creativity, can this ordinary garden be turned into an otherworldly escape, all on a £5,000 budget? James, who has Asperger’s syndrome, has been living independently in his own home since the passing of their father in 2021. His sister Maria and her husband live just a mile away, and together they form a close-knit and supportive family. James’s lifelong passion for classic Doctor Who and all things sci-fi has inspired this ambitious project, a fun, thematic garden where he can relax, enjoy nature and truly feel at home in his very own alien world.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Anna, Gemma, Zoe and Andreas – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns - but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Ria Lina. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: After solving the Andie Bell case, Pip is forced to confront the consequences of what her investigation exposed. It may have cleared Sal’s name, but it tore Cara’s family apart, and the guilt weighs heavily on Pip. In an attempt to rebuild her relationship with Cara, Pip releases a podcast to tell the world the real story. The only person yet to face justice is Max Hastings, and as his trial approaches, Pip is determined to help his victims find closure. However, the prosecution’s case begins to falter when Becca Bell withdraws from testifying. Unwilling to accept this, Pip musters the courage to visit Becca in prison with the hope of convincing her that giving evidence still matters. Pip wants to focus on supporting Ravi at the upcoming memorial for his brother, but when a mysterious note promising information on Max appears in her locker, Pip must make a difficult decision. Little Kilton comes together to say goodbye to both Andie Bell and Sal Singh. The end of one dark chapter gives way to another, as Cara finds herself in a dangerous situation, and Jamie Reynolds, Connor’s brother and a key witness in Max’s trial, disappears without warning.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip hits a dead end and rethinks. Digging into Jamie’s recent behaviour and last movements, she realises he may not be an innocent victim after all.

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon, Lee Mack and David Mitchell return in an episode packed with some of the best bits from series 19. A stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal amazing stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Among the guests joining Lee Mack and David Mitchell are Lucy Beaumont, Bob Mortimer, Jamelia, John Kearns, Harriet Kemsley, Yinka Bokinni, Gyles Brandreth, Dianne Buswell, Mark Chapman, Montell Douglas, Tasha Ghouri, Julie Hesmondhalgh, Will Kirk, David Morrissey, Josh Pugh and Holly Willoughby.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is overcome by the amount of beige on show in a Telford flat. Dion heads downwards to reveal an unexpected bonus in Leeds. In Suffolk, there are character features for Jacqui to uncover.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: A well-groomed Charlie Ross pays a visit to a barbershop museum in Norfolk to see a huge collection of antique shaving mugs. One scuttle-shaped mug was patented in around 1867. In total, proud museum owner Richard Finney has 500 on display. Aiming to shave off a few pounds on their purchases are two teams of families shopping at a massive antiques centre in King’s Lynn. In red are father and daughter Simon and Ellen, and in blue are father and son Dave and James. With maths teacher Ellen keeping tabs on the reds’ budget, scientist Simon hopes their chemistry will generate profits. Meanwhile, the blues have a close encounter with a model of E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, but at £245, he’s not coming home with them. Wielding his gavel in neighbouring Lincolnshire is auctioneer Colin Young. He shares his estimates with Charlie before the teams’ items go under the hammer. Profit or loss, one team comes out on top – but which one?

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie and Flo head to Shrewsbury to help James and his sister Maria transform his plain, uninspired garden into a Doctor Who-inspired sci-fi dream. With little more than a fence, a small shed and a table and chairs, the space is ready for a complete regeneration! A lifelong Doctor Who and sci-fi fan, James envisions a low-maintenance, alien-themed haven complete with a TARDIS-style shed, futuristic planting, a circular pathway and a tranquil water feature. With Maria’s support and Charlie and Flo’s creativity, can this ordinary garden be turned into an otherworldly escape, all on a £5,000 budget? James, who has Asperger’s syndrome, has been living independently in his own home since the passing of their father in 2021. His sister Maria and her husband live just a mile away, and together they form a close-knit and supportive family. James’s lifelong passion for classic Doctor Who and all things sci-fi has inspired this ambitious project, a fun, thematic garden where he can relax, enjoy nature and truly feel at home in his very own alien world.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Anna, Gemma, Zoe and Andreas – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: After solving the Andie Bell case, Pip is forced to confront the consequences of what her investigation exposed. It may have cleared Sal’s name, but it tore Cara’s family apart, and the guilt weighs heavily on Pip. In an attempt to rebuild her relationship with Cara, Pip releases a podcast to tell the world the real story. The only person yet to face justice is Max Hastings, and as his trial approaches, Pip is determined to help his victims find closure. However, the prosecution’s case begins to falter when Becca Bell withdraws from testifying. Unwilling to accept this, Pip musters the courage to visit Becca in prison with the hope of convincing her that giving evidence still matters. Pip wants to focus on supporting Ravi at the upcoming memorial for his brother, but when a mysterious note promising information on Max appears in her locker, Pip must make a difficult decision. Little Kilton comes together to say goodbye to both Andie Bell and Sal Singh. The end of one dark chapter gives way to another, as Cara finds herself in a dangerous situation, and Jamie Reynolds, Connor’s brother and a key witness in Max’s trial, disappears without warning.

One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: A well-groomed Charlie Ross pays a visit to a barbershop museum in Norfolk to see a huge collection of antique shaving mugs. One scuttle-shaped mug was patented in around 1867. In total, proud museum owner Richard Finney has 500 on display. Aiming to shave off a few pounds on their purchases are two teams of families shopping at a massive antiques centre in King’s Lynn. In red are father and daughter Simon and Ellen, and in blue are father and son Dave and James. With maths teacher Ellen keeping tabs on the reds’ budget, scientist Simon hopes their chemistry will generate profits. Meanwhile, the blues have a close encounter with a model of E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, but at £245, he’s not coming home with them. Wielding his gavel in neighbouring Lincolnshire is auctioneer Colin Young. He shares his estimates with Charlie before the teams’ items go under the hammer. Profit or loss, one team comes out on top – but which one?

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie and Flo head to Shrewsbury to help James and his sister Maria transform his plain, uninspired garden into a Doctor Who-inspired sci-fi dream. With little more than a fence, a small shed and a table and chairs, the space is ready for a complete regeneration! A lifelong Doctor Who and sci-fi fan, James envisions a low-maintenance, alien-themed haven complete with a TARDIS-style shed, futuristic planting, a circular pathway and a tranquil water feature. With Maria’s support and Charlie and Flo’s creativity, can this ordinary garden be turned into an otherworldly escape, all on a £5,000 budget? James, who has Asperger’s syndrome, has been living independently in his own home since the passing of their father in 2021. His sister Maria and her husband live just a mile away, and together they form a close-knit and supportive family. James’s lifelong passion for classic Doctor Who and all things sci-fi has inspired this ambitious project, a fun, thematic garden where he can relax, enjoy nature and truly feel at home in his very own alien world.

programme.title: Breakfast

programme.title: Morning Live
programme.desc: Morning Live is BBC One’s flagship daytime programme, bringing you the best advice from familiar faces across the BBC, original journalism and investigations, and a sparkle of Strictly magic

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: When a viewer contacts Rip Off Britain after suspecting the online task work he’s been completing might not be for real, the team investigate the sophisticated world of so-called task scams. Plus justice for the victims of one dodgy spray foam insulation firm. Seven years after Rip Off Britain went undercover as a sales operative, the team hear how that footage formed part of the investigation that put the man responsible behind bars.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is overcome by the amount of beige on show in a Telford flat. Dion heads downwards to reveal an unexpected bonus in Leeds. In Suffolk, there are character features for Jacqui to uncover.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: A well-groomed Charlie Ross pays a visit to a barbershop museum in Norfolk to see a huge collection of antique shaving mugs. One scuttle-shaped mug was patented in around 1867. In total, proud museum owner Richard Finney has 500 on display. Aiming to shave off a few pounds on their purchases are two teams of families shopping at a massive antiques centre in King’s Lynn. In red are father and daughter Simon and Ellen, and in blue are father and son Dave and James. With maths teacher Ellen keeping tabs on the reds’ budget, scientist Simon hopes their chemistry will generate profits. Meanwhile, the blues have a close encounter with a model of E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, but at £245, he’s not coming home with them. Wielding his gavel in neighbouring Lincolnshire is auctioneer Colin Young. He shares his estimates with Charlie before the teams’ items go under the hammer. Profit or loss, one team comes out on top – but which one?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Natalie Cassidy: Caring Together
programme.desc: Natalie’s juggling college and family life, learning about teenage mental health, online pressures and autism - and how care reaches far beyond the classroom.

programme.title: Robson Green's Weekend Escapes
programme.desc: The Rev Richard Coles joins Robson to explore the Northumberland coastline. They take a Canadian canoe trip along the River Coquet, visit the hidden gem of Walkworth's secret hermitage, make the crossing to Lindisfarne for a photography class and have a go at rope work.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: In Somerset, Micky from the busy seaside town of Hove is ready to fulfil a long-held dream of escaping to the countryside. She wants a property with lots of land for her big, beloved rescue dog, and Jules Hudson is there to answer her prayers with a line-up of standout properties that fit the bill. Jules also tries his hand at traditional screen printing when he visits a small studio specialising in designs inspired by nature.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie and Flo head to Shrewsbury to help James and his sister Maria transform his plain, uninspired garden into a Doctor Who-inspired sci-fi dream. With little more than a fence, a small shed and a table and chairs, the space is ready for a complete regeneration! A lifelong Doctor Who and sci-fi fan, James envisions a low-maintenance, alien-themed haven complete with a TARDIS-style shed, futuristic planting, a circular pathway and a tranquil water feature. With Maria’s support and Charlie and Flo’s creativity, can this ordinary garden be turned into an otherworldly escape, all on a £5,000 budget? James, who has Asperger’s syndrome, has been living independently in his own home since the passing of their father in 2021. His sister Maria and her husband live just a mile away, and together they form a close-knit and supportive family. James’s lifelong passion for classic Doctor Who and all things sci-fi has inspired this ambitious project, a fun, thematic garden where he can relax, enjoy nature and truly feel at home in his very own alien world.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Anna, Gemma, Zoe and Andreas – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: The brainy quiz returns - but this time host Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Ria Lina. As always, contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: MasterChef

programme.title: Amandaland

programme.title: Spotlight
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, weather and features from the South West of England.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: After solving the Andie Bell case, Pip is forced to confront the consequences of what her investigation exposed. It may have cleared Sal’s name, but it tore Cara’s family apart, and the guilt weighs heavily on Pip. In an attempt to rebuild her relationship with Cara, Pip releases a podcast to tell the world the real story. The only person yet to face justice is Max Hastings, and as his trial approaches, Pip is determined to help his victims find closure. However, the prosecution’s case begins to falter when Becca Bell withdraws from testifying. Unwilling to accept this, Pip musters the courage to visit Becca in prison with the hope of convincing her that giving evidence still matters. Pip wants to focus on supporting Ravi at the upcoming memorial for his brother, but when a mysterious note promising information on Max appears in her locker, Pip must make a difficult decision. Little Kilton comes together to say goodbye to both Andie Bell and Sal Singh. The end of one dark chapter gives way to another, as Cara finds herself in a dangerous situation, and Jamie Reynolds, Connor’s brother and a key witness in Max’s trial, disappears without warning.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: Pip hits a dead end and rethinks. Digging into Jamie’s recent behaviour and last movements, she realises he may not be an innocent victim after all.

programme.title: Would I Lie to You?
programme.desc: Rob Brydon, Lee Mack and David Mitchell return in an episode packed with some of the best bits from series 19. A stellar cast of celebrity guests reveal amazing stories about themselves. But are they telling the truth, or are they making it all up? Among the guests joining Lee Mack and David Mitchell are Lucy Beaumont, Bob Mortimer, Jamelia, John Kearns, Harriet Kemsley, Yinka Bokinni, Gyles Brandreth, Dianne Buswell, Mark Chapman, Montell Douglas, Tasha Ghouri, Julie Hesmondhalgh, Will Kirk, David Morrissey, Josh Pugh and Holly Willoughby.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: A well-groomed Charlie Ross pays a visit to a barbershop museum in Norfolk to see a huge collection of antique shaving mugs. One scuttle-shaped mug was patented in around 1867. In total, proud museum owner Richard Finney has 500 on display. Aiming to shave off a few pounds on their purchases are two teams of families shopping at a massive antiques centre in King’s Lynn. programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: In Somerset, Micky from the busy seaside town of Hove is ready to fulfil a long-held dream of escaping to the countryside. She wants a property with lots of land for her big, beloved rescue dog, and Jules Hudson is there to answer her prayers with a line-up of standout properties that fit the bill. Jules also tries his hand at traditional screen printing when he visits a small studio specialising in designs inspired by nature.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie and Flo head to Shrewsbury to help James and his sister Maria transform his plain, uninspired garden into a Doctor Who-inspired sci-fi dream. With little more than a fence, a small shed and a table and chairs, the space is ready for a complete regeneration! A lifelong Doctor Who and sci-fi fan, James envisions a low-maintenance, alien-themed haven complete with a TARDIS-style shed, futuristic planting, a circular pathway and a tranquil water feature. With Maria’s support and Charlie and Flo’s creativity, can this ordinary garden be turned into an otherworldly escape, all on a £5,000 budget? James, who has Asperger’s syndrome, has been living independently in his own home since the passing of their father in 2021. His sister Maria and her husband live just a mile away, and together they form a close-knit and supportive family. James’s lifelong passion for classic Doctor Who and all things sci-fi has inspired this ambitious project, a fun, thematic garden where he can relax, enjoy nature and truly feel at home in his very own alien world.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Anna, Gemma, Zoe and Andreas – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: A well-groomed Charlie Ross pays a visit to a barbershop museum in Norfolk to see a huge collection of antique shaving mugs. One scuttle-shaped mug was patented in around 1867. In total, proud museum owner Richard Finney has 500 on display. Aiming to shave off a few pounds on their purchases are two teams of families shopping at a massive antiques centre in King’s Lynn. With maths teacher Ellen keeping tabs on the reds’ budget, scientist Simon hopes their chemistry will generate profits. Profit or loss, one team comes out on top – but which one?

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: In Somerset, Micky from the busy seaside town of Hove is ready to fulfil a long-held dream of escaping to the countryside. programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Charlie and Flo head to Shrewsbury to help James and his sister Maria transform his plain, uninspired garden into a Doctor Who-inspired sci-fi dream. With little more than a fence, a small shed and a table and chairs, the space is ready for a complete regeneration! A lifelong Doctor Who and sci-fi fan, James envisions a low-maintenance, alien-themed haven complete with a TARDIS-style shed, futuristic planting, a circular pathway and a tranquil water feature. With Maria’s support and Charlie and Flo’s creativity, can this ordinary garden be turned into an otherworldly escape, all on a £5,000 budget? James, who has Asperger’s syndrome, has been living independently in his own home since the passing of their father in 2021. His sister Maria and her husband live just a mile away, and together they form a close-knit and supportive family. James’s lifelong passion for classic Doctor Who and all things sci-fi has inspired this ambitious project, a fun, thematic garden where he can relax, enjoy nature and truly feel at home in his very own alien world.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Anna, Gemma, Zoe and Andreas – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: After solving the Andie Bell case, Pip is forced to confront the consequences of what her investigation exposed. It may have cleared Sal’s name, but it tore Cara’s family apart, and the guilt weighs heavily on Pip. In an attempt to rebuild her relationship with Cara, Pip releases a podcast to tell the world the real story. The only person yet to face justice is Max Hastings, and as his trial approaches, Pip is determined to help his victims find closure. However, the prosecution’s case begins to falter when Becca Bell withdraws from testifying. Unwilling to accept this, Pip musters the courage to visit Becca in prison with the hope of convincing her that giving evidence still matters. Pip wants to focus on supporting Ravi at the upcoming memorial for his brother, but when a mysterious note promising information on Max appears in her locker, Pip must make a difficult decision. Little Kilton comes together to say goodbye to both Andie Bell and Sal Singh. The end of one dark chapter gives way to another, as Cara finds herself in a dangerous situation, and Jamie Reynolds, Connor’s brother and a key witness in Max’s trial, disappears without warning.

programme.title: Food Fest Scotland
programme.desc: Edith Bowman and Colin Murray explore the food stalls and events at the Peebles Show. They discover tips and treats from passionate food producers, from perfect steaks to creating premium chocolate at a fraction of the price. Farmer Jim Smith is near Inverness discovering the story behind every bag of carrots, and chef Julie Lin investigates what we’re missing out on when it comes to mackerel.

programme.title: Born to Be Wild
programme.desc: The orphan season at the SSPCA Rescue Centre continues with the admission of a brood of tiny orphaned squirrels. With bald skins and closed eyes, they are among the smallest that have ever been admitted to the centre. It’s down to wildlife assistant Juanita to take on the job of rearing them by hand, but there is help from April, the acting head of large mammals. Juanita names them after birds, and soon, Goose, Puffin, Noddy, Dodo and co are off on their rewilding journey at the centre. Meanwhile, in the sea-bird area, the team are dealing with a pair of feisty young characters - Noodles and Big Mac are a pair of orphaned gannets full of ‘teenage’ attitude. However, that doesn’t phase their carers, Gaby and Kaniz, who are determined to get them back to the wil.

programme.desc: Sixty rides and £100 million of equipment – Kirkcaldy Links Market is the pinnacle of the showmen calendar. programme.title: Showpeople: Licensed to Thrill
programme.desc: Lovebirds Margaret and Randall have been married for over 50 years. But when it came time to retire, the couple just couldn’t leave the showman life behind, so they packed up their bags and rejoined the fair. Meanwhile, young actor and showman Bailey has also made a career decision – he will be venturing on stage to try his hand at stand-up comedy. And for Christian Horne, the wet and windy summer means he is taking advantage of the big event of the season – Euro 2024.

programme.title: Teen Predator/Online Killer
programme.desc: As police piece together the last few minutes of Cimarron’s life, they realise McCartney was still online threatening her when she tragically shot herself. Police and prosecutors move quickly to establish if there’s a case for manslaughter. Police from Northern Ireland travel to West Virginia to conduct the manslaughter investigation, where they learn that Cimarron’s own family had no idea why she took her own life. In a tragic turn, they learn that 18 months after her death, Cimarron’s father had also died by suicide. In order to charge McCartney with manslaughter, the police have to prove that he foresaw the risk to her life. As they comb through the cyber evidence from his devices, they build a case for manslaughter and charge him. The case sets new legal precedent in the UK. More than five years after the police investigation began, McCartney is finally convicted and sentenced.

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: Calamity James is a slapstick comedy about a young man, James, who is cursed with ‘acute misfortune syndrome’. James tries to reconnect with his dad after being thrown out by his mum for setting fire to their house at a family barbecue. In this world, chronic bad luck exists and the unbelievable is the everyday.

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: Life is hard, so Callum and Jordan, two emotionally unassembled young lads from Northern Ireland, start the Funboys’ Fun Club: a playgroup for childish young men to engage in wholesome mucking about. But when a juice party goes awry, Callum’s ultra-religious fiancée Morgan kicks them out, and the Funboys must search for a new HQ. When they come across Marty, a catatonically depressed 60-year-old, can they bring joy back to his life and prove that fun won't necessarily lead to an eternity spent in raging hellfire?

programme.title: Louis Theroux
programme.desc: Louis explores how America has managed to take our darkest desires, commodify them and turn them into a saleable product. From his memorable Weird Weekends episodes on porn and rap to films about Las Vegas and the US opioid crisis, this episode explores a very human tendency to jump to the dark side when seeking out pleasure – whether through indulgence, risk-taking or the joy of doing something seen as ‘bad’ or 'wrong’. Louis re-connects with porn-star JJ, who over 20 years ago was just making his way in the adult industry but has since turned his back on that world in favour of a new life in eastern Europe. And Louis catches up once more with Katilia from Heroin Town, whom he last saw hopelessly addicted to drugs, with little sign of turning her life around.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Two dog-loving developers tackle epic projects in Wales and Norfolk. Also, a seasoned developer is looking to move quickly and economically in Nottingham.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s Belgian rail journey continues in the Dutch speaking region of Flanders. In Antwerp, he discovers the city's historic multibillion-pound diamond industry and drops in at the workshop of an expert. Just outside the city, Michael boards the Dendermonde to Puurs Heritage Railway, run by volunteers, and gets a chance to drive one of its 1950s diesel engines. Heading to Belgium’s third city, Ghent, Michael visits the magnificent cathedral and marvels at a 15th-century Van Eyck masterpiece, the Adoration of the Mystic Lamb, the most stolen painting in the world.

programme.title: Great Japanese Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael takes a luxury, panoramic Shimikaze train to the beautiful Shima Peninsula. It transports visitors to Ise Jingu, Japan’s most sacred Shinto shrine, and is also renowned for its stunning coastline. Michael takes a trip to Ago Bay, where over 60 small islands sit just off the coast in the shimmering Pacific Ocean. The next stop is Nara, the ancient capital of Japan, a beautiful, tranquil city where some 1,400 sika deer roam the green open spaces. Michael visits the magnificent Buddhist Todaiji temple and is astonished to find one of the largest bronze Buddha statues in the world, towering at a height of 15 metres. Michael’s last stop in Nara is at a traditional sumi stick workshop. Made from soot, gelatine and perfume, these blocks of ink are used for Japanese calligraphy.

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Leaving Seoul aboard South Korea’s high-speed KTX train, Michael travels south through the heart of the country to explore how rail has shaped both its economy and identity. His first stop is Daejeon, a centre of science and education, where a local bakery founded by a North Korean refugee offers a small but telling story of postwar resilience. Nearby, in Geumsan, Michael visits a ginseng research institute to discover how Korea’s most prized root, cultivated for over 1,500 years, has evolved from traditional medicine into a global health and skincare industry. Continuing east along the historic Gyeongbu line, Michael learns how Korea’s railways, first laid at the end of the 19th century, became the backbone of the modern nation. In Gyeongju, the ancient capital of the Silla dynasty, he joins archaeologists excavating royal burial mounds, uncovering gold artefacts that reveal the story of Korea’s first unification. The journey ends in Busan, where Michael explores a hillside community built by war refugees and meets an artist whose work reflects the city’s enduring legacy of displacement, creativity and renewal.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: The unique quiz show where if a player gives an Impossible answer, they are immediately eliminated. Which of the 24 contestants will face the £10,000 question today?

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: The hunt for the nation's Mastermind continues as Clive Myrie tests four more contenders on their specialist subjects and general knowledge. This time, the subjects are the jazz pianist Bill Evans, Georges Remi and Tintin, William Morris, and Torchwood.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Under the Vines
programme.desc: Gus and Tippy are lost in their own dilemmas, while Daisy, still hurting over her argument with Griffin, struggles to get everyone on track to complete the showcase preparations in time. Louis receives a distressing phone call, but Rowan arrives to deliver a surprise that brings both shock and relief. Meanwhile, Daisy involves herself in Tippy’s mysterious behaviour, which leads them to bond over Stanley’s memory, and Louis finds himself uncomfortable when he’s roped in to take part in a rabbit hunt, which leads to some bonding of his own. Daisy has a wake-up call over her relationship status with Ben when Marissa ups her competitive game.

programme.title: The Secret Life of Elephants
programme.desc: First in a series of three programmes revealing the emotional and dramatic lives of elephants in Kenya's Samburu reserve. As the day begins, there is great excitement in one elephant family when a new baby, named Breeze, is born. But her first few weeks look set to be the most dangerous of her life. Meanwhile, elephant experts Iain and Saba Douglas-Hamilton face the huge challenge of fitting a radio collar to a three-tonne female elephant with an entire herd looking out for her. Breeze faces her first big test, crossing a river, and the research team investigate when one of their best-known bull elephants is found dead in suspicious circumstances. Back in the reserve, a young calf becomes injured and cannot keep up with his herd. His mother sticks with him, but will he survive without the support of a family? There is further tragedy when a matriarch dies. In unique footage, a herd of elephants visit her body, and appear to mourn her death.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team of experts invite another selection of people to bring along their antiques for valuation, this time at Warwick Castle. Items include a particularly strange cigar lighter, a model guillotine made by French prisoners of war and a life drawing of spectacular quality.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from historic St Albans Cathedral and Abbey in Hertfordshire. Antiques experts Claire Rawle and Jonathan Pratt find a selection of antiques and collectibles to take to auction. Claire discovers an arts and crafts bowl which may have belonged to George Bernard Shaw's wife, and Jonathan gets excited when he finds a drawing by the artist Dame Laura Knight. Paul Martin takes a trip underground to explore the intriguing Royston Cave, which boasts medieval carvings.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Cheryl Baker, Chris Bavin, Axel Blake and Sophie Willan take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Continuing his Belgian tour, Michael Portillo heads to the beach resort of Knokke-Heist and the world’s longest coastal tram, which enjoys splendid views across the North Sea, to trace its roots back to the 19th-century beginnings of tourism. He visits the Port of Zeebrugge, which was attacked by the British in 1918 when the country was occupied by the Germans. Further along the coast on the Dutch border, Michael explores the salt marshes and mud flats of the Zwin Nature Reserve, home to 300 species of birds, and helps to track their migration habits. And continuing to the medieval city of Bruges, Michael visits a saxophone maker and discovers how the instrument, so crucial to the development of jazz, was invented in Belgium.

programme.title: Iolo's River Valleys
programme.desc: Iolo explores the stunning Dee valley, from wintering birds along the estuary to displaying black grouse on moorland, rare freshwater-pearl mussels and spawning sea trout.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Hannah explores whether the death of privacy puts society at greater risk or could make people safer.

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Modern Life
programme.desc: Hannah takes a look at the air fryer – a device that is rapidly taking over people's kitchens, cooking up everything from bread rolls to baked Alaska and almost making ovens obsolete. Hannah dives into its surprising history, going behind the scenes with air fryer originators Philips. She discovers how the accidental creation of a wonder wire in the 1900s, a WWII pilot’s cold dinner and one man tinkering in his garage created this modern marvel that is redefining cooking.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham, Michaela Strachan and the team are live from the National Trust's Crom Estate as nature writes its own stories, with triumph, heartbreak and surprise around every corner. The live remote cameras are capturing fledging, predation and drama around the clock, from otters on the lough shore to red squirrels in ancient woodland. Meanwhile, Iolo Williams remains at the Knepp rewilding estate in Sussex, where he takes a look the lives of some of the country's rarest species.

programme.title: Surgeons: At the Edge of Life
programme.desc: Surgeons drain all of their patient’s blood from his body to replace damaged arteries. A patient’s fertility is at risk without a complex operation to remove diseased bowel.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: On patrol in the city centre, Adam and Nigel receive reports of men fleeing police. As they round the corner, they spot them legging it. Adam takes pursuit, tackles and detains one of the suspects. A few minutes later, unbelievably, he must do it again, as the man bursts out of the police car, trying to escape. Back at the station, Anna and Perri can’t resist the temptation to hide the boss’s car, temporarily. Meanwhile, the whole team leap into action when a stolen car fails to stop for Adam. When the driver runs off, Dave relies on his years of experience and pays a visit to a serial car thief matching the driver’s description. While the Peelers wait for CCTV footage to come in, the suspect tells Stephen about his prolific criminal past, his hatred of police and struggles with addiction.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: Unspun World with John Simpson
programme.desc: Unspun World provides an unvarnished version of the week's major global news stories - reliable, honest and essential viewing. The BBC's world affairs editor, John Simpson, brings his experience and expertise to bear on the most important international stories. In discussion with the BBC's unparalleled range of experts across the world, he uses their unique local knowledge to go beyond the headlines to get to the unspun truth about the world.

programme.title: Dark Waters
programme.desc: Past ties drag corporate lawyer Rob into conflict with a company blamed for polluting a local stream. But as the case goes on, Rob discovers that the scope of the actual damage is staggeringly vast.

programme.title: Surgeons: At the Edge of Life
programme.desc: A surgeon must remove part of his patient’s tongue and reconstruct it to save her from an aggressive cancer, and surgeons perform a rare simultaneous pancreas and kidney transplant.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Two dog-loving developers tackle epic projects in Wales and Norfolk. Also, a seasoned developer is looking to move quickly and economically in Nottingham.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s Belgian rail journey continues in the Dutch speaking region of Flanders. In Antwerp, he discovers the city's historic multibillion-pound diamond industry and drops in at the workshop of an expert. Just outside the city, Michael boards the Dendermonde to Puurs Heritage Railway, run by volunteers, and gets a chance to drive one of its 1950s diesel engines. Heading to Belgium’s third city, Ghent, Michael visits the magnificent cathedral and marvels at a 15th-century Van Eyck masterpiece, the Adoration of the Mystic Lamb, the most stolen painting in the world.

programme.title: Great Japanese Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael takes a luxury, panoramic Shimikaze train to the beautiful Shima Peninsula. It transports visitors to Ise Jingu, Japan’s most sacred Shinto shrine, and is also renowned for its stunning coastline. Michael takes a trip to Ago Bay, where over 60 small islands sit just off the coast in the shimmering Pacific Ocean. The next stop is Nara, the ancient capital of Japan, a beautiful, tranquil city where some 1,400 sika deer roam the green open spaces. Michael visits the magnificent Buddhist Todaiji temple and is astonished to find one of the largest bronze Buddha statues in the world, towering at a height of 15 metres. Michael’s last stop in Nara is at a traditional sumi stick workshop. Made from soot, gelatine and perfume, these blocks of ink are used for Japanese calligraphy.

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Leaving Seoul aboard South Korea’s high-speed KTX train, Michael travels south through the heart of the country to explore how rail has shaped both its economy and identity. His first stop is Daejeon, a centre of science and education, where a local bakery founded by a North Korean refugee offers a small but telling story of postwar resilience. Nearby, in Geumsan, Michael visits a ginseng research institute to discover how Korea’s most prized root, cultivated for over 1,500 years, has evolved from traditional medicine into a global health and skincare industry. Continuing east along the historic Gyeongbu line, Michael learns how Korea’s railways, first laid at the end of the 19th century, became the backbone of the modern nation. In Gyeongju, the ancient capital of the Silla dynasty, he joins archaeologists excavating royal burial mounds, uncovering gold artefacts that reveal the story of Korea’s first unification. The journey ends in Busan, where Michael explores a hillside community built by war refugees and meets an artist whose work reflects the city’s enduring legacy of displacement, creativity and renewal.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: The unique quiz show where if a player gives an Impossible answer, they are immediately eliminated. Which of the 24 contestants will face the £10,000 question today?

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: The hunt for the nation's Mastermind continues as Clive Myrie tests four more contenders on their specialist subjects and general knowledge. This time, the subjects are the jazz pianist Bill Evans, Georges Remi and Tintin, William Morris, and Torchwood.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Under the Vines
programme.desc: Gus and Tippy are lost in their own dilemmas, while Daisy, still hurting over her argument with Griffin, struggles to get everyone on track to complete the showcase preparations in time. Louis receives a distressing phone call, but Rowan arrives to deliver a surprise that brings both shock and relief. Meanwhile, Daisy involves herself in Tippy’s mysterious behaviour, which leads them to bond over Stanley’s memory, and Louis finds himself uncomfortable when he’s roped in to take part in a rabbit hunt, which leads to some bonding of his own. Daisy has a wake-up call over her relationship status with Ben when Marissa ups her competitive game.

programme.title: The Secret Life of Elephants
programme.desc: First in a series of three programmes revealing the emotional and dramatic lives of elephants in Kenya's Samburu reserve. As the day begins, there is great excitement in one elephant family when a new baby, named Breeze, is born. But her first few weeks look set to be the most dangerous of her life. Meanwhile, elephant experts Iain and Saba Douglas-Hamilton face the huge challenge of fitting a radio collar to a three-tonne female elephant with an entire herd looking out for her. Breeze faces her first big test, crossing a river, and the research team investigate when one of their best-known bull elephants is found dead in suspicious circumstances. Back in the reserve, a young calf becomes injured and cannot keep up with his herd. His mother sticks with him, but will he survive without the support of a family? There is further tragedy when a matriarch dies. In unique footage, a herd of elephants visit her body, and appear to mourn her death.
