Back in the reserve, a young calf becomes injured and cannot keep up with his herd. His mother sticks with him, but will he survive without the support of a family? There is further tragedy when a matriarch dies. In unique footage, a herd of elephants visit her body, and appear to mourn her death.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the team of experts invite another selection of people to bring along their antiques for valuation, this time at Warwick Castle. Items include a particularly strange cigar lighter, a model guillotine made by French prisoners of war and a life drawing of spectacular quality.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Flog It! comes from historic St Albans Cathedral and Abbey in Hertfordshire. Antiques experts Claire Rawle and Jonathan Pratt find a selection of antiques and collectibles to take to auction. Claire discovers an arts and crafts bowl which may have belonged to George Bernard Shaw's wife, and Jonathan gets excited when he finds a drawing by the artist Dame Laura Knight. Paul Martin takes a trip underground to explore the intriguing Royston Cave, which boasts medieval carvings.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Cheryl Baker, Chris Bavin, Axel Blake and Sophie Willan take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Continuing his Belgian tour, Michael Portillo heads to the beach resort of Knokke-Heist and the world’s longest coastal tram, which enjoys splendid views across the North Sea, to trace its roots back to the 19th-century beginnings of tourism. He visits the Port of Zeebrugge, which was attacked by the British in 1918 when the country was occupied by the Germans. Further along the coast on the Dutch border, Michael explores the salt marshes and mud flats of the Zwin Nature Reserve, home to 300 species of birds, and helps to track their migration habits. And continuing to the medieval city of Bruges, Michael visits a saxophone maker and discovers how the instrument, so crucial to the development of jazz, was invented in Belgium.

programme.title: Iolo's River Valleys
programme.desc: Iolo explores the stunning Dee valley, from wintering birds along the estuary to displaying black grouse on moorland, rare freshwater-pearl mussels and spawning sea trout.

programme.title: The Future with Hannah Fry
programme.desc: Hannah explores whether the death of privacy puts society at greater risk or could make people safer.

programme.title: The Secret Genius of Modern Life
programme.desc: Hannah takes a look at the air fryer – a device that is rapidly taking over people's kitchens, cooking up everything from bread rolls to baked Alaska and almost making ovens obsolete. Hannah dives into its surprising history, going behind the scenes with air fryer originators Philips. She discovers how the accidental creation of a wonder wire in the 1900s, a WWII pilot’s cold dinner and one man tinkering in his garage created this modern marvel that is redefining cooking.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham, Michaela Strachan and the team are live from the National Trust's Crom Estate as nature writes its own stories, with triumph, heartbreak and surprise around every corner. The live remote cameras are capturing fledging, predation and drama around the clock, from otters on the lough shore to red squirrels in ancient woodland. Meanwhile, Iolo Williams remains at the Knepp rewilding estate in Sussex, where he takes a look the lives of some of the country's rarest species.

programme.title: Surgeons: At the Edge of Life
programme.desc: Surgeons drain all of their patient’s blood from his body to replace damaged arteries. A patient’s fertility is at risk without a complex operation to remove diseased bowel.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: On patrol in the city centre, Adam and Nigel receive reports of men fleeing police. As they round the corner, they spot them legging it. Adam takes pursuit, tackles and detains one of the suspects. A few minutes later, unbelievably, he must do it again, as the man bursts out of the police car, trying to escape. Back at the station, Anna and Perri can’t resist the temptation to hide the boss’s car, temporarily. Meanwhile, the whole team leap into action when a stolen car fails to stop for Adam. When the driver runs off, Dave relies on his years of experience and pays a visit to a serial car thief matching the driver’s description. While the Peelers wait for CCTV footage to come in, the suspect tells Stephen about his prolific criminal past, his hatred of police and struggles with addiction.

programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: Unspun World with John Simpson
programme.desc: Unspun World provides an unvarnished version of the week's major global news stories - reliable, honest and essential viewing. The BBC's world affairs editor, John Simpson, brings his experience and expertise to bear on the most important international stories. In discussion with the BBC's unparalleled range of experts across the world, he uses their unique local knowledge to go beyond the headlines to get to the unspun truth about the world.

programme.title: Dark Waters
programme.desc: Past ties drag corporate lawyer Rob into conflict with a company blamed for polluting a local stream. But as the case goes on, Rob discovers that the scope of the actual damage is staggeringly vast.

programme.title: Surgeons: At the Edge of Life
programme.desc: A surgeon must remove part of his patient’s tongue and reconstruct it to save her from an aggressive cancer, and surgeons perform a rare simultaneous pancreas and kidney transplant.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Two dog-loving developers tackle epic projects in Wales and Norfolk. Also, a seasoned developer is looking to move quickly and economically in Nottingham.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s Belgian rail journey continues in the Dutch speaking region of Flanders. In Antwerp, he discovers the city's historic multibillion-pound diamond industry and drops in at the workshop of an expert. Just outside the city, Michael boards the Dendermonde to Puurs Heritage Railway, run by volunteers, and gets a chance to drive one of its 1950s diesel engines. Heading to Belgium’s third city, Ghent, Michael visits the magnificent cathedral and marvels at a 15th-century Van Eyck masterpiece, the Adoration of the Mystic Lamb, the most stolen painting in the world.

programme.title: Great Japanese Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael takes a luxury, panoramic Shimikaze train to the beautiful Shima Peninsula. It transports visitors to Ise Jingu, Japan’s most sacred Shinto shrine, and is also renowned for its stunning coastline. Michael takes a trip to Ago Bay, where over 60 small islands sit just off the coast in the shimmering Pacific Ocean. The next stop is Nara, the ancient capital of Japan, a beautiful, tranquil city where some 1,400 sika deer roam the green open spaces. Michael visits the magnificent Buddhist Todaiji temple and is astonished to find one of the largest bronze Buddha statues in the world, towering at a height of 15 metres. Michael’s last stop in Nara is at a traditional sumi stick workshop. Made from soot, gelatine and perfume, these blocks of ink are used for Japanese calligraphy.

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Leaving Seoul aboard South Korea’s high-speed KTX train, Michael travels south through the heart of the country to explore how rail has shaped both its economy and identity. His first stop is Daejeon, a centre of science and education, where a local bakery founded by a North Korean refugee offers a small but telling story of postwar resilience. Nearby, in Geumsan, Michael visits a ginseng research institute to discover how Korea’s most prized root, cultivated for over 1,500 years, has evolved from traditional medicine into a global health and skincare industry. Continuing east along the historic Gyeongbu line, Michael learns how Korea’s railways, first laid at the end of the 19th century, became the backbone of the modern nation. In Gyeongju, the ancient capital of the Silla dynasty, he joins archaeologists excavating royal burial mounds, uncovering gold artefacts that reveal the story of Korea’s first unification. The journey ends in Busan, where Michael explores a hillside community built by war refugees and meets an artist whose work reflects the city’s enduring legacy of displacement, creativity and renewal.

Evil Pea threatens to cut them down again, so Supertato and Carrot turn their kites into hang-gliders and embark on an epic aerial chase with Evil Pea, leading to her bursting her balloon on a chopsticks display sign. Supertato and Carrot land safely on the ground, ready to fly kites again!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing and Sula are performing a puppet show for Flop, Amma and Pando when Coco and Charlie arrive. Coco wants to join in with her Rainbow Fairy Mice. Sula tells a frustrated Bing that you have to be loud when you do a show. But Bing is a little too loud, and when Coco joins the show, Bing's loud Biteysaurus isn't welcome, as he is hurting Sula’s ears!

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Mojo’s got the perfect top for digging up the bones of a Swoppitus Rex. But could an actual dinosaur still be alive under Jackson’s field, or is it a case of mistaken identity?

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Betty recalls the first time she pushed the red button, the Squirrels explore a range of emotions with Happy, Angry Bull tells a not-so-sleepy bedtime story, and the gerbils sing.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: After overhearing Duggee listening to a beautiful track by the Squirrel Valley Voices Choir, the Squirrels seek to learn more about the roles that make up a choir – basses, sopranos, altos and tenors. A distressed Eugene then alerts them that half of the choir have been taken sick and can’t perform that day. The Squirrels step up to take their place. Initially, when the newly arranged choir sing, the voices aren’t gelling together. Duggee teaches them the principles they must get right first, for the choir to succeed – breathing, pitch, volume, focus and timing. With a lot of practice, the Squirrels turn up to perform perfectly together and finally earn their Choir Badge.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bingo finds a toy turtle at the playground and wants to take him home.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bingo is convinced that she has ruined Mother's Day when she drops Mum’s breakfast in bed on the floor. But Bluey helps make amends by putting on a play about how Mum and Dad first met.

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: Ubercorn is excited to see the northern lights, but Glitch's Grunge-Grimbler covers them with smoke.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Old Brown takes Peter's journal, Peter must choose between holding on to his most precious possession and saving a friend.

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: Animated deep sea adventure series. Captain Barnacles and his intrepid band of explorers roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. The Octonauts help clean up a beach after a storm, but things get complicated when the resident fiddler crabs hijack the Gup-D!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: One and her chums carefully cross the pattern puzzle paths over the magic moats to get to the Pattern Palace. Learn about patterns with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: A, N and T sit down for a nice picnic, but soon everyone is getting tickled, the food starts disappearing and N gets the blame. This episode has fun with consonant clusters and the words ant, ants, pants, pans, taps, snap and picnic.

programme.title: Nick Cope's Popcast
programme.desc: Nick is performing at a special birthday party and needs a poptastic list of songs to sing. He can’t believe his eyes when the birthday girl calls up to check on the list, and together they write today’s Popcast song.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Billy and Sillies perform a little hoedown to the tune of Hey Diddle Diddle.

programme.title: Playtime Towers
programme.desc: Where is Bella hiding? Maybe behind her big, colourful towel! Lift and Bella play games with the towel, and together they set off to explore the floors of Playtime Towers. In the Sing Song Forest, Tincy has spotted a towel and bathtub in her web, perfect for a rub-a-dub singsong! Kingsley and Queenie relax on their beach towels in the Fortress of Fun and decide to play a game of ‘Big Sunglasses, Little Sunglasses’. In the Ice Disco, Hettie the Yeti makes up a new dance with the Playtimers called the Butterfly Boogie.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Flop teaches Bing and Pando how to blow bubbles. Pando soon gets the hang of it, but Bing struggles and gets frustrated. Finally, Bing blows a big bubble and is outraged when Pando pops it.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘rocket’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. We explore all sorts of rockets – a big rocket, a tiny rocket and a shiny rocket. We see a blast off rocket, a flying rocket and a rocket zooming to the moon. There’s even a banana rocket! The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch
programme.desc: Barnaby gets upset when he can't contribute to Lu's silly soup.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Kiri and Lou try out being trees, which is mostly about keeping still, and make a very large new friend named Moa.

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: Ziff, Pipp and Button don their spacesuits to become the first frogs to walk on the moon.

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are at the seaside, where they see a man getting ready to go swimming. He has a beach tent, and they see him putting some things inside it (his straw hat and suntan lotion) before he sets off towards the water. The Twirlywoos decide to put more of the man's things inside the tent, starting with small things like a book and progressing to larger and sillier objects, including a deckchair and an inflatable dolphin! The man comes back from his swim and is surprised to discover his tent stuffed full of all his possessions. The Twirlywoos have left their tea things out, and Peekaboo comes out to explore them. There is a little bit of tea left in the teapot, and Peekaboo tries to get it by squeezing right inside the teapot. He then drinks the tea - only to find that there is no way out! The Twirlywoos return, and Peekaboo tries to run past them. They chase the runaway teapot all around the boat until Peekaboo manages to give them the slip and get back to the hole in the wall. As Peekaboo squeezes inside the hole, the teapot pops off and lands back on the tea table.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin’s friend teaches him about celebrating Eid and together they enjoy a big feast. The Tumbles are also preparing a meal, but there’s one guest who can’t wait to start eating.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po are outside in the cold when they spot the Tiddlytubbies who are inside and warm. The Teletubbies put on hats, gloves and scarves to keep warm.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Nigel and Baby Bear welcome babies Elias, Eliza, Billie, Enya, Isobel, Teddy and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Parents, carers and their babies at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are plastic tubs which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding baby appropriate plastic tub inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The popular nursery rhyme ‘A Sailor Went to Sea’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Action Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children play doctor with dolls, learning British Sign Language signs for doctor, sick and bed, then sing and sign Miss Polly Had a Dolly.

programme.title: I Can Grow It
programme.desc: With spring in full swing, the garden is really starting to flourish, and it’s not just the flowers and trees that are blossoming! Admiring all the colourful flowers, Aaron, Joda and Isla come across some mysterious plants growing from the ground. But what could they be? It’s time to call in Chatterpot!

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: Rebecca and Murphi are trying to come up with a new move to perfect their competition dance routine. They take a break for an ice-cold monster shake and find time to create a bottle penguin. The Mini Monsters demonstrate how to make everlasting sandcastles, and Rebecca’s aunt calls from space - where she has made some alien friends. The Recycling Express arrives with empty tissue boxes, inspiring a mega monster make – a funny pineapple puppet.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: It's the day when the Potatodons' hides are extra hot, crispy and delicious!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey is running a taxi service. Her first passenger is Businessman Dad, who is in a rush to get to the airport. But with unexpected delays, Dad's in danger of missing his flight!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels see Duggee reading Wonderful Stories about Wise Animals and want to learn about wisdom and how they can become wiser. They find out that wisdom isn’t just about facts and figures, but that it's about good judgement and experiences too. They learn to plan ahead, concentrate on the task at hand, that sometimes big problems need a little help, to focus on the present and that good things come to those who wait. Thank goodness Duggee is so wise!

programme.title: Let's Go for a Walk
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers walk through the gardens in the city to the bus stop to catch a bus. On the way they have a concert under a giant spiderweb, sit on a woolly bench, spot a rollercoaster and even wash a giant greenhouse!

programme.title: My First Festivals
programme.desc: Following seven-year-old Iqra as she and her family prepare for the celebration Eid (Eid Al-Adha). With lots of things to do before the big day, Iqra starts her journey by visiting her local mosque to meet the Imam to find out more about Eid. Traditionally, family members get each other a secret gift for Eid. After buying a secret present for her dad and a new dress, she joins her mum and grandma and helps them to cook up some delicious, special food for her community. Once the day arrives, Iqra heads over to her grandma’s to join the rest of her family as they all come together to feast and celebrate Eid together.

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Brunsli biscuits are a traditional Swiss recipe that taste and smell very Christmassy. Tilly adds spices such as ground nutmeg to her chocolate biscuit dough, before cutting it into snowflake shapes. With the help of her sister, Tilly decorates her biscuits with a beautiful white icing. Tilly's table has lots of Christmas decorations on it as well as the traditional flower of Switzerland, edelweiss. Let's hope Tilly's friends enjoy the taste of the biscuits!

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: Maddie is at a building site and finds out how tracks work to help a digger move up and down mounds of earth. Maddie wears some special shoe attachments to show us how the digger’s tracks work to stop it sinking into the soil. Then she attaches a special camera to the digger – to see it in action as it lifts the soil high into the dumper truck! Next, she visits a wellie factory to see how wellies are made. Maddie uses her special cameras to see how the PVC material is injected into the wellie moulds – a bit like making a jelly! We find out how a different colour is injected to make the sole before they are squashed together to make a complete colourful wellie.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Guide dog Kika and her owner Dr Amit are off to the Sticks 'n’ Stuff shop with Amit’s friend Alana, who is also blind, to help her buy a new white cane.

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie head into the heat of the butterfly house to meet the owl butterfly. They discover that this giant butterfly gets its name from the distinct patterns on its wings, which look just like an owl’s eye. Next, Aneeshwar and Lizzie visit another winged animal, the sunbittern. They find out that this beautiful bird is an expert hunter who stalks riverbanks, standing perfectly still to catch fish. Finally, Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the wild connection is between these two incredible animals.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle won’t move from his new doggy doormat because he loves it very much. Jess opens the door to reveal Gram and Grand have come to visit and Grand has made coconut cake for everyone plus a special cake for Waffle but Waffle won’t move from his doggy door mat to greet him. Gram and Grand discover that Waffle can talk and Evie tells them Waffle’s learning to read, too. Gram gives Waffle a congratulatory snuggle and Waffle loves it!

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Mossy? A hero?

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: It’s been raining, and Toad is resisting the urge to join in with Yukee and her friends' game of musical mud-squelching. However, he can’t resist the muddy beat and is soon squelching with his friends.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Mum takes Maddie and Triggs to McGinty's annual sports day. But when Triggs is selected to take part in the obstacle race, he soon realises that it's all about winning and not about having fun. With Maddie's help, Triggs tries to show the other competitors that having fun with your friends is more important than winning.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are out doing their exercises when suddenly, a cheetah called Chipo comes along with his dance crew. He criticises them for not being able to dance in time, and it turns out Duggee used to be part of the dance crew! Duggee was a great dancer, but he never stuck to the choreography and was always making up his own moves.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Children's animation. Five is so good at hide-and-seek, she can find the others without looking up from her book - but how? Learn how to add to five.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. From A to Z, every Alphablock has fun discovering the magic of wordplay. P, A, R, T and Y need some help getting the party started! S tries her best, but they really need someone extraordinary to liven things up and superhero Exciting X soon gets the party popping with his special powers.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Maddie meets Kian and Monroe at the park, where they gather natural materials together. Mr Tumble gets messy trying to paint a picture. The spotty surprise combines art and nature as everyone makes their own portrait using the natural materials they have found in the park. Featuring signs for the words stick, picture and flower.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Tinky Winky, Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po run around in circles in the Home Dome. The Noo-noo joins in and the Teletubbies have fun chasing.

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers discover how wild flower meadows play an important role in the environment. They find out that both big and small patches of wild flowers can be great wildlife corridors for creatures to move around safely and that they are great for pollinators like bees and butterflies. On the way, they pretend to be animals living in the meadow and enjoy relaxing amongst the lovely flowers.

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: Elvis has forgotten his trainers and has to wear a pair with laces, but he can’t tie them without his gran’s help. He needs to quickly learn to tie them himself if he wants to get a PB.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: In this episode, Grace shows off three amazing machines that all belong on the beach. Grace uses a very special machine to launch a lifeboat, shows off a machine that helps scientists and drives a sea tractor.

programme.title: Dodge's Pup School
programme.desc: Dodge is determined to win the Class Star award, but with Cherry winning every week for being a superstar at everything, it’s going to be tough! Dodge, Woofer and Jazz try to hatch a plan, but when Jazz and Dodge get swept up in their ideas, like getting Miss Collie a gift, they ignore Woofer’s advice that there’s a better way. Dodge brings Miss Collie a gift into the classroom from the playground and chaos ensues, leaving Dodge with no hope of winning the class star. Dodge discovers that the real key to winning is by trying his best.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the baby Pea-Rexes must teach a lost baby Bokchoydactyl how to fly.

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: Tracker finds trapped creatures in an underground tunnel after falling into a sinkhole.

But with his father's journal and the help of his best friends Benjamin and Lily, Peter is ready for some fun and delightful new discoveries. When Old Brown catches their friend Jack Sharp, Peter, Lily and Benjamin must race to return this fish-out-of-water to the lake!

programme.desc: The Squirrels have just got some new walkie-talkies and are having so much fun with them. Communicating through his walkie-talkie, Tag doesn’t know where he is. He can see lots and lots of things around him but no one has any idea where this room is in the house!

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Sunny is nervous that Baby Mouse will get hurt when she starts to take her first steps.

programme.title: Supertato

programme.desc: Nori and Dot are stuck in a treehouse without a door. How can Mojo and Bo get them out? By sending the treehouse flying across town, that’s how!

programme.desc: Waffle is at Mrs Hobbs’ house until the Brooklyn-Bells return from holiday. He acts like a cat to please her and helpfully washes up his bowl, but accidentally leaves the taps on.

programme.desc: Rafi and Aunty T visit the Manchester Museum. Rafi thinks dinosaurs are more than fine and wishes for a real one. Suddenly, Slurpy the triceratops appears! Slurpy is cheeky - he slurps faces, leaves colourful footprints and knocks things over while munching salad. Rafi worries about the mess, but Aunty T laughs and enjoys the fun. When the wish ends, Slurpy disappears, and Aunty T uses her own wand to put the museum back together. She admits dinosaurs and museums are magic, and Rafi beams with delight.

Navid saves their fish for them, and JoJo learns that the market is just like a family – the people are kind and look out for each other.

programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Sarah needs some new shoes, but picks out a very unusual pair.

programme.desc: Major invents a Clanger finder, but it is not very useful – it always finds the Clanger who is holding it. Major is disappointed – he hadn't thought of that. But Granny comes up with a better suggestion to keep him busy: he could mend their clock, which hasn't worked for some time. Major Clanger has a think, then brightens up immediately. He can do better than that – he will build a new clock, and it will be his best invention ever. But it turns out the others don't agree.

programme.title: When English Football Ruled Europe
programme.desc: This two-part documentary series examines the years between 1977 and 1984 when English football dominated the European Cup - featuring interviews with the stars of the victorious teams, the series reveals the remarkable stories behind the triumphs and explains how some of the most colourful characters in the game mastered Europe's foremost club competition. This part covers Bob Paisley's Liverpool, who sealed their first win in the competition in 1977 and retained the trophy the next year. The mantle then passed to Nottingham Forest - inspired by the charismatic Brian Clough, they dumped Liverpool out of the competition and went on to win back-to-back trophies themselves in what was a phenomenal achievement for a club of their size.

programme.title: When English Football Ruled Europe
programme.desc: This two-part documentary series examines the years between 1977 and 1984 when English football dominated the European Cup - featuring interviews with the stars of the victorious teams, the series reveals the remarkable stories behind the triumphs and explains how some of the most colourful characters in the game mastered Europe's foremost club competition. This part covers Bob Paisley's Liverpool, who sealed their first win in the competition in 1977 and retained the trophy the next year. The mantle then passed to Nottingham Forest - inspired by the charismatic Brian Clough, they dumped Liverpool out of the competition and went on to win back-to-back trophies themselves in what was a phenomenal achievement for a club of their size.

programme.title: When English Football Ruled Europe
programme.desc: This two-part documentary series examines the years between 1977 and 1984 when English football dominated the European Cup - featuring interviews with the stars of the victorious teams, the series reveals the remarkable stories behind the triumphs and explains how some of the most colourful characters in the game mastered Europe's foremost club competition. This part covers Bob Paisley's Liverpool, who sealed their first win in the competition in 1977 and retained the trophy the next year. The mantle then passed to Nottingham Forest - inspired by the charismatic Brian Clough, they dumped Liverpool out of the competition and went on to win back-to-back trophies themselves in what was a phenomenal achievement for a club of their size.

programme.title: When English Football Ruled Europe
programme.desc: This two-part documentary series examines the years between 1977 and 1984 when English football dominated the European Cup - featuring interviews with the stars of the victorious teams, the series reveals the remarkable stories behind the triumphs and explains how some of the most colourful characters in the game mastered Europe's foremost club competition. This part covers Bob Paisley's Liverpool, who sealed their first win in the competition in 1977 and retained the trophy the next year. The mantle then passed to Nottingham Forest - inspired by the charismatic Brian Clough, they dumped Liverpool out of the competition and went on to win back-to-back trophies themselves in what was a phenomenal achievement for a club of their size.

programme.desc: Crime drama. A brutal robbery at a secluded Brighton house pulls Grace and Branson into a challenging enquiry when thousands of pounds worth of beautiful antiques are stolen and the owner is left fighting for her life - the prime target, however, appears to have been an item of great sentimental value to the homeowner and her brother who is a renowned antiques dealer. This particular item has deep emotional ties to a fascinating mystery involving their father which spans back to 1960s East London and a painful night on which their life as they knew it changed forever - as Grace digs deeper into this mysterious crime, he unearths a web of ancient grudges which leads him down a murderous trail through the world of Brighton antiques in a race against time to discover who is at the heart of this robbery, recover what was taken, and bring to light answers which have been buried for many years.

When the dead body of their photographer turns up onsite, it throws the business into disarray - their shop is a crime scene and everyone is a suspect. The victim is soon connected to the theft of a local diamond from a previous shoot - with his wallet gone, it's possible someone knew about the diamond. Elsewhere, Geordie tries to track down Alphy's mother despite Alphy not wanting to meet her - Geordie figures it can't hurt to try without Alphy knowing, but when Cathy raises a glass to Geordie finding Alphy's mum after the fashion show, this is the first that Alphy has heard of it and he is forced to react in front of everyone.

programme.desc: Herman the Postman is going on holidays. He has left his round to the young Steart O'Meara, who hasn't yet encountered all of Garfield's devilish traps...

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: It's winter and Garfield and his friends, Odie and Nermal, are competing for the price of "the best Christmas carolling singer". There are cookies at stake!

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Jon's cousin has passed away and has left his fortune to Jon and Doc Boy. But there's one condition: the one who will spend an entire night in a spooky manor will be the one to inherit everything.

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: After Garfield slightly changes the recipe of Odie's birthday cake, it comes to life and spreads panic in town!

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Garfield has been mean to Odie again. Left in the garden, he's taken in by a neighbour, Nathan. Odie is happy with this new friendship, but he soon discovers that Garfield wasn't that bad after all...

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Garfield takes us through the ages to tell us the history of dogs. As we know, he has a poor opinion of them, but an incident will make him change his mind. After all, all dogs are not useless!

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Garfield is bored. He has nothing to do. Well, not exactly: watching Odie and the squirrels in the garden, there's fun ahead after all!

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Eddie Gourmand has built a super attraction park, made completely out of cheese. Squeak and his friends beg Garfield to take them there but with Harry working as a security guard, it won't be easy!

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Pooky has disappeared again, but this time, it's Nermal who finds it. He is willing to give it back to him at one condition: Garfield has to be really nice to Nermal for the rest of the day!

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Garfield's cat instincts push him to climb on a tree. But how will he get down? Everyone tries to give him a hand, but they end up stuck in that tree! Now he's out on a limb; who will save him?

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Nermal doesn't believe in super heroes. Garfield does and he tries desperately to convince him. Even if that means disguising himself as Ultra Powerful Guy.

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Garfield receives a strange helmet which lets him read everyone's thoughts. He even catches aliens' conversations who are just about to conquer Earth! Garfield has to stop this plot immediately!

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: After Odie dreams of being a super hero, Garfield mocks him for it. But when Garfield really gets into trouble, Odie puts his grudges aside and flies off to help him. And this time he REALLY flies!

programme.title: The Garfield Show
programme.desc: Nermal makes a bet with Garfield: if Garfield manages not to eat for a whole hour, he won't see Nermal for a whole month. Will Garfield be victorious ?

programme.title: The Garfield Show
